paragraphs: Limble sells a computerized maintenance management system for the teams that keep equipment and facilities running. The pitch is simpler work orders, assets that keep running and more productivity across every site. The company says it is rated number one by more than 50,000 maintenance professionals.

A work order can start from a dashboard, an asset record or a vendor, with details and photos added from a phone. Anyone in the organization can submit a request by scanning a QR code or visiting a URL, with no account required. Preventive maintenance is scheduled automatically on time, usage or condition. Parts inventory triggers push and email alerts when stock runs low. The mobile app keeps working without a signal and syncs once the device reconnects. Listed integrations include SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and QuickBooks Online.

Public sector users shown include a city water treatment plant in Lompoc. The company says a team at the City of Albuquerque was confidently using the mobile app after one day of training. It reports a 4.8 out of 5 rating on G2 and Capterra from well over 1,400 combined verified reviews. It also says customers typically see value in about three weeks.

quote.text: Simplify work orders, keep assets running smoothly, and increase productivity across every site.
